dimensions.assessment: Affects state and territorial peace officer standards and training agencies, law enforcement hiring bodies, and the FBI.
dimensions.evidence: authorizes a new type of entity—peace officer standards and training agencies—to access criminal history record information maintained by the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

dimensions.assessment: Gives these agencies direct access to federal background check and criminal history records for employment and licensing evaluations.
dimensions.evidence: set standards for the hiring, training, ethical conduct, and retention of the law enforcement officers of the State

dimensions.assessment: The source material does not provide specific figures on federal spending or revenue changes.
Amends federal statute regarding information exchange and requires the Attorney General to amend federal regulations.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Attorney General shall amend part 20 of title 28, Code of Federal Regulations

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent statutory changes to FBI record-sharing authorities.
dimensions.evidence: Section 534 of title 28, United States Code, is amended

missing_information: No explicit fiscal cost or budget impact data is provided.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill allows peace officer standards and training agencies across states and territories to access FBI criminal history records, altering information-sharing rules and requiring federal regulation updates.
